items.item_text: A valid CA Driver's License may be required.
Medical Office Service Coordinator (MOSC) OR Patient Service Rep (PSR)

The Medical Office Service Coordinators are responsible for providing optimum medical support services to patients, families and internal medical colleagues. Incumbents perform a variety of clinical/patient support functions which may involve activities such as computer system operations, medical office reception work using EMR Systems (EPIC), patient scheduling, registration, pre-admission, admission, and discharge and coordination of services.  Medical records maintenance, verification of insurance, referral and authorization coordination, case management, cashiering duties, telephone coordination and general support to staff.
(11/20/2026 at 11:59pm); Interviews and recruiting process may occur at any time
Minimum 6 months experience with front office reception and patient registration
Experience verifying insurance, processing authorizations and referrals
Knowledge of practices and protocols related to medical office procedures, (i.e. medical terminology, appointments, medical records, insurance verification, cashiering, billing, etc.)
Experience with an electronic health record (EHR), or electronic medical (EMR) system, EPIC a plus!
Knowledge of all pertinent laws, regulations, and guidelines governing medical records; confidentiality, privacy, and provision to others, including HIPAA.

Knowledge of health care insurance systems, which may include Medi-Cal, Medicare, HMO, PPO, fee-for-service, county funded coverage, and workers' compensation, to properly obtain and track authorizations, appoint patients, make referrals for consults, diagnostics and ancillary services,
Experience coordinating hospital services, completing and submitting billing documentation, and explaining provisions and requirements to patients.

Temporary Employment Services provides temporary employees to various departments throughout UC Davis Campus in Davis and UC Davis Health Campus in Sacramento, at the request of the departments. Employees can elect to be considered for assignments on either or both campuses although most medical office positions will be located in the Sacramento area. The available assignments can be full-time, and short-term or long-term in duration. Medical Office Service Coordinators, Hospital Unit Service Coordinators and Patient Access Representatives are limited to 5.5 months.

Interpersonal skills to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all co-workers; to consistently interact with patients and other members of the public with patience, courtesy, and professionalism, both in person and on the telephone; and to effectively respond to individuals who may be angry or upset.

Organizational skills to establish priorities for own work within stated guidelines; respond flexibly to changes in priorities; and maintain work effectiveness in a setting with a high volume of patient activity and frequent interruptions.
Knowledge of ICD-9, CPT and HCPCS coding to identify services performed, including diagnoses, procedures, and supplies.
Filing skills to maintain logs and files of information in alphabetical, chronological and/or numerical order, such that it is current and easily retrievable.
